eg: She is studying for a degree in economics at a university in Manchester.
egCn: 她正在曼彻斯特的一所大学攻读经济学学位。

eg: Many students who graduate from university still struggle to find a suitable job.
egCn: 许多大学毕业生仍然很难找到合适的工作。

eg: Without proper qualifications, it is hard to get a well-paid job these days.
egCn: 如今没有像样的学历证书，很难找到高薪工作。

eg: Attending lectures is useful, but students also need time to read on their own.
egCn: 听讲座很有用，但学生也需要时间自主阅读。

eg: After finishing the six-month course, every participant receives a certificate.
egCn: 完成六个月的课程后，每位学员都会获得一份证书。

eg: In my country, children usually start primary school at the age of six.
egCn: 在我们国家，孩子通常六岁上小学。

eg: Smaller classes allow teachers to give each pupil more individual attention.
egCn: 小班教学能让老师给每个学生更多的个别关注。

eg: Some parents send their children to kindergarten as early as three years old.
egCn: 有些父母早在孩子三岁时就送他们去幼儿园。

eg: Some students care more about getting high grades than actually understanding the subject.
egCn: 有些学生更在意拿高分，而不是真正理解这门学科。

eg: Teachers should not rely only on textbooks but also use real-life examples.
egCn: 教师不应只依赖课本，还应使用现实生活中的例子。

eg: Students often memorise facts for exams and then forget them a week later.
egCn: 学生常常为考试死记硬背一些知识点，一周后就忘了。

eg: Most teenagers in Britain leave secondary school at sixteen or eighteen.
egCn: 英国大多数青少年在十六岁或十八岁时中学毕业离校。

eg: She won a full scholarship, so she did not have to pay any tuition fees.
egCn: 她获得了全额奖学金，所以不用交任何学费。

eg: Strict discipline in schools may improve behaviour but can also reduce creativity.
egCn: 学校严格的纪律或许能改善学生行为，但也可能削弱创造力。

eg: Many people believe that financial skills should be part of the school curriculum.
egCn: 许多人认为理财技能应该纳入学校课程。

eg: More adults are enrolling on evening courses to improve their job prospects.
egCn: 越来越多的成年人报名参加夜校课程，以改善就业前景。

eg: Undergraduates at this university must complete a research project in their final year.
egCn: 这所大学的本科生必须在最后一年完成一个研究项目。

eg: Students who leave their assignments until the last minute often produce weaker work.
egCn: 把作业拖到最后一刻的学生，交上来的作业质量往往较差。

eg: In many countries, education is compulsory until the age of sixteen.
egCn: 在许多国家，十六岁前的教育都是义务教育。

eg: Some students drop out of university because they cannot afford the living costs.
egCn: 有些学生因负担不起生活费而从大学退学。

eg: Children at boarding school learn to be independent but may miss their families.
egCn: 上寄宿学校的孩子能学会独立，但可能会想家。

eg: Access to higher education should depend on ability, not on family income.
egCn: 能否接受高等教育应取决于能力，而非家庭收入。

eg: Distance learning allows working adults to study without giving up their jobs.
egCn: 远程教育让在职成年人无需辞职就能学习。

cn: 家庭教师；（大学）导师；辅导教师
eg: Wealthy families often hire a private tutor to help their children prepare for exams.
egCn: 富裕家庭常请私人家教帮助孩子备考。

eg: Living on campus makes it easier for first-year students to make new friends.
egCn: 住在校园里让大一新生更容易交到新朋友。

eg: Students should not be forced to specialise in one subject too early.
egCn: 不应强迫学生过早地专攻某一门学科。

cn: 男校或女校；单一性别学校
eg: Some parents believe girls achieve better results in single-sex schools.
egCn: 有些家长认为女生在女校里成绩更好。

eg: The government should spend more money on state schools in poorer areas.
egCn: 政府应该在较贫困地区的公立学校上投入更多资金。

eg: The school introduced free breakfasts and saw a clear rise in attendance.
egCn: 学校推出免费早餐后，出勤率明显上升。

eg: A well-educated workforce helps a country compete in the global economy.
egCn: 受过良好教育的劳动力有助于一个国家在全球经济中竞争。

eg: Vocational courses give young people practical skills that employers actually need.
egCn: 职业课程能让年轻人掌握雇主真正需要的实用技能。

eg: Extracurricular activities such as sport and music help children build confidence.
egCn: 体育、音乐等课外活动能帮助孩子建立自信。

cn: 读写能力；（某领域的）基本知识和能力
eg: Improving adult literacy can help people find better jobs and support their children.
egCn: 提高成人读写能力能帮助人们找到更好的工作并辅导孩子。

eg: Rising tuition fees discourage many students from poorer backgrounds from applying to university.
egCn: 不断上涨的学费让许多家境较差的学生不敢申请大学。

eg: In a fast-changing job market, lifelong learning is no longer optional.
egCn: 在快速变化的就业市场中，终身学习已不再是可有可无的。

eg: Schools should teach critical thinking so that students can question what they read online.
egCn: 学校应该培养批判性思维，让学生能对网上读到的内容提出质疑。

eg: The history syllabus focuses heavily on dates rather than on understanding causes.
egCn: 历史教学大纲过于侧重年代，而不是对历史成因的理解。

cn: 间隔年（中学毕业后、上大学前的休学年）
eg: Taking a gap year to work or travel can help young people mature.
egCn: 用间隔年去工作或旅行能帮助年轻人变得更成熟。

eg: Teenagers often start smoking because of peer pressure rather than personal choice.
egCn: 青少年开始吸烟往往是因为同伴压力，而不是个人选择。

eg: Critics argue that rote learning produces good exam results but little real understanding.
egCn: 批评者认为，死记硬背能带来好的考试成绩，却难以带来真正的理解。

cn: 薪水；工资（通常按月或按年计）
eg: A high salary is attractive, but job satisfaction matters just as much to many people.
egCn: 高薪很有吸引力，但对许多人来说，工作满意度同样重要。

eg: Many young people now change careers several times during their working lives.
egCn: 如今许多年轻人在职业生涯中会多次转行。

eg: Employers increasingly value communication skills as much as technical knowledge.
egCn: 雇主越来越重视沟通能力，其看重程度不亚于专业知识。

eg: Companies that treat their employees well usually have lower staff turnover.
egCn: 善待员工的公司通常人员流动率较低。

eg: Getting along with colleagues makes even a stressful job much more enjoyable.
egCn: 和同事相处融洽，即使压力大的工作也会愉快得多。

eg: He worked long hours for three years before he finally got a promotion.
egCn: 他连续三年长时间工作，终于获得了晋升。

eg: Dressing smartly for a job interview shows respect for the employer.
egCn: 求职面试时穿着得体，是对雇主的尊重。

eg: In many countries, people are now expected to retire later than their parents did.
egCn: 在许多国家，人们现在需要比父辈更晚退休。

eg: Having a part-time job teaches students how to manage both time and money.
egCn: 做兼职工作能教会学生如何管理时间和金钱。

eg: Doing too much overtime can damage both your health and your family life.
egCn: 加班太多会损害你的健康和家庭生活。

eg: Being unemployed for a long time can seriously affect a person's confidence.
egCn: 长期失业会严重打击一个人的自信心。

eg: The restaurant is short of staff, so the waiters often work twelve-hour shifts.
egCn: 这家餐厅人手不足，服务员经常要上十二小时的班。

cn: 工资（通常按小时或周计）
eg: Raising the minimum wage would help low-paid workers cover basic living costs.
egCn: 提高最低工资将帮助低收入工人负担基本生活开支。

eg: With people living longer, governments are struggling to pay everyone a decent pension.
egCn: 随着人们寿命延长，政府越来越难给每个人发放体面的养老金。

eg: She resigned from her job because she wanted to start her own business.
egCn: 她辞去了工作，因为她想自己创业。

eg: Youth unemployment remains high in regions where traditional industries have closed down.
egCn: 在传统产业已经关闭的地区，青年失业率依然居高不下。

eg: Constant pressure to meet deadlines is one of the main causes of stress at work.
egCn: 不断赶截止日期的压力是工作压力的主要来源之一。

eg: Teachers complain that their workload has increased while their pay has stayed the same.
egCn: 教师们抱怨工作量增加了，而工资却没变。

eg: The manager was dismissed after he was caught taking money from the company.
egCn: 这名经理因被发现挪用公司钱款而遭解雇。

eg: Working the night shift for years can disturb a person's sleep patterns.
egCn: 常年上夜班会扰乱一个人的睡眠规律。

eg: Rural schools find it difficult to recruit and keep experienced teachers.
egCn: 农村学校很难招聘并留住有经验的教师。

eg: The company interviewed twenty candidates before choosing someone with international experience.
egCn: 公司面试了二十名求职者，最后选了一位有国际经验的人。

eg: There are plenty of vacancies in the care sector, but the pay is low.
egCn: 护理行业有很多职位空缺，但薪水很低。

eg: Being self-employed gives you freedom, but your income may be less stable.
egCn: 自己当老板很自由，但收入可能不太稳定。

eg: Bullying in the workplace should be taken as seriously as bullying at school.
egCn: 职场霸凌应该和校园霸凌一样受到重视。

eg: The trade union is demanding better pay and safer working conditions for its members.
egCn: 工会正在为其会员争取更高的工资和更安全的工作条件。

cn: 熟练的；有技能的；需要技能的
eg: There is a growing shortage of skilled workers such as plumbers and electricians.
egCn: 水管工、电工等熟练技术工人日益短缺。

cn: 主管；监督人；（研究生）导师
eg: A good supervisor gives clear feedback and helps new staff develop their skills.
egCn: 好的主管会给出明确的反馈，并帮助新员工提升技能。

eg: Group projects at school are a good way to develop teamwork and leadership.
egCn: 学校的小组项目是培养团队合作和领导能力的好方法。

eg: Many artists find it hard to earn a living from their work alone.
egCn: 许多艺术家很难仅靠自己的作品谋生。

cn: 被裁员的；多余的；累赘的
eg: Hundreds of factory workers were made redundant when the plant moved abroad.
egCn: 工厂迁往国外后，数百名工人被裁员。

eg: Freelance designers can choose their own clients but have no paid holidays.
egCn: 自由职业的设计师可以自己挑客户，但没有带薪假期。

eg: Flexible working hours can help parents achieve a better work-life balance.
egCn: 弹性工作时间能帮助父母更好地平衡工作与生活。

eg: Older workers often value job security more than a higher salary.
egCn: 年长的员工往往更看重工作稳定，而不是更高的薪水。

eg: Recognition from managers often increases job satisfaction more than extra money does.
egCn: 上司的认可往往比额外的钱更能提升工作满意度。

eg: Young entrepreneurs need access to cheap loans to turn their ideas into businesses.
egCn: 年轻创业者需要获得低息贷款，才能把想法变成生意。

cn: 生产率；生产力；工作效率
eg: Some firms found that a four-day week did not reduce productivity at all.
egCn: 一些公司发现，每周工作四天根本没有降低生产率。

eg: Women now make up almost half of the workforce in many developed countries.
egCn: 在许多发达国家，女性现在几乎占劳动力的一半。

eg: An apprenticeship lets young people earn money while learning a trade.
egCn: 学徒制让年轻人可以边学手艺边挣钱。

cn: 玻璃天花板（阻碍女性或少数群体晋升的无形障碍）
eg: Although more women are managers today, many still hit a glass ceiling before reaching the top.
egCn: 虽然如今女性管理者增多了，但许多人在升到高层之前仍会碰到玻璃天花板。

eg: Some criminals return to crime because they cannot find work after prison.
egCn: 有些罪犯出狱后找不到工作，于是重新犯罪。

eg: The robbery took place in broad daylight outside a busy shopping centre.
egCn: 这起抢劫案发生在一家繁忙的购物中心外，而且是光天化日之下。

eg: Harsher punishment does not always reduce crime if offenders expect not to be caught.
egCn: 如果罪犯认为自己不会被抓，更严厉的惩罚也未必能减少犯罪。

eg: Police arrested three teenagers for damaging cars in the town centre.
egCn: 警方逮捕了三名在市中心破坏汽车的青少年。

eg: The case will go to court next month, and both drivers must give evidence.
egCn: 此案下月将开庭审理，两名司机都必须出庭作证。

eg: If he is found guilty, he could spend up to five years in prison.
egCn: 如果他被判有罪，可能要坐牢五年。

eg: Although murder is rare in the city, people still worry about their safety at night.
egCn: 虽然这座城市很少发生谋杀案，人们晚上仍担心自身安全。

eg: Drivers who use their phones while driving should face a large fine.
egCn: 开车时使用手机的司机应被处以高额罚款。

eg: Some parents worry that violent video games make children more aggressive.
egCn: 一些家长担心暴力电子游戏会让孩子更具攻击性。

eg: In some countries, it is illegal to sell alcohol to anyone under twenty-one.
egCn: 在一些国家，向未满二十一岁的人出售酒类是违法的。

eg: Sending young offenders to prison may turn them into more serious criminals.
egCn: 把青少年罪犯送进监狱，可能会让他们变成更严重的罪犯。

eg: Victims of crime should receive emotional support as well as financial compensation.
egCn: 犯罪受害者除了经济补偿，还应获得情感支持。

eg: People who commit a crime for the first time deserve a second chance.
egCn: 初次犯罪的人应该得到第二次机会。
collocations: be accused of committing a crime

eg: Dropping litter is a minor offence, but it is still punished with a fine.
egCn: 乱扔垃圾虽是轻微违法，但仍会被罚款。

eg: Burglary rates usually rise in winter when houses are dark and empty for longer.
egCn: 冬天房屋天黑得早、空置时间长，入室盗窃率通常会上升。

eg: A witness saw the man running from the shop and called the police.
egCn: 一名目击者看到那名男子从店里跑出来，随即报了警。

eg: The judge gave him a two-year sentence for driving without a licence.
egCn: 法官因他无证驾驶判处他两年徒刑。

eg: The suspect was questioned for six hours before being released without charge.
egCn: 嫌疑人被问讯了六个小时，之后未被起诉便获释放。

eg: Everyone accused of a crime has the right to a fair trial.
egCn: 每个被控犯罪的人都有权获得公正审判。

eg: In law, a person is considered innocent until proven guilty.
egCn: 在法律上，一个人在被证明有罪之前都被视为无辜的。

eg: The politician was accused of accepting money from a large construction company.
egCn: 这位政客被指控收受一家大型建筑公司的钱。

eg: The crime rate fell after the council installed better street lighting.
egCn: 市议会改善街道照明后，犯罪率下降了。

eg: Shoplifting is often committed by young people looking for excitement rather than money.
egCn: 商店偷窃往往是寻求刺激而非图钱的年轻人所为。

eg: Supporters of the death penalty claim it stops people from committing serious crimes.
egCn: 死刑的支持者声称它能阻止人们犯下严重罪行。

eg: The families of victims often say they want justice, not revenge.
egCn: 受害者家属常说，他们要的是公道，而不是报复。

eg: Bicycle theft is a common problem in many university towns.
egCn: 自行车被盗是许多大学城的常见问题。

eg: The businessman was kidnapped and held for ransom for nearly two weeks.
egCn: 这位商人遭绑架，被扣押索要赎金将近两周。

eg: After three days of discussion, the jury decided that the woman was not guilty.
egCn: 经过三天讨论，陪审团裁定这名女子无罪。

eg: Youth clubs give teenagers somewhere safe to go instead of joining gangs.
egCn: 青少年俱乐部给了青少年一个安全的去处，让他们不去加入帮派。

cn: 社区服务（一种替代监禁的刑罚）
eg: Instead of going to prison, minor offenders could do community service such as cleaning parks.
egCn: 轻罪犯人可以做清扫公园之类的社区服务，而不是坐牢。

eg: Young offenders should be given education and training rather than long prison terms.
egCn: 应该给青少年罪犯提供教育和培训，而不是判处长期徒刑。

eg: Elderly people are often the main targets of telephone fraud.
egCn: 老年人往往是电话诈骗的主要目标。

eg: Long prison sentences may not be an effective deterrent for young offenders.
egCn: 长期徒刑对青少年罪犯未必能起到有效的威慑作用。

eg: Prisons should focus on rehabilitation so that inmates can live normal lives after release.
egCn: 监狱应注重改造，让服刑人员出狱后能过正常生活。

cn: 青少年的；未成年的；幼稚的
eg: Juvenile crime is often linked to poverty, poor schooling and family problems.
egCn: 青少年犯罪往往与贫困、教育不良和家庭问题有关。

eg: Shops have the right to prosecute anyone caught stealing, whatever their age.
egCn: 商店有权起诉任何被抓到偷窃的人，无论其年龄大小。

eg: Most citizens are law-abiding and simply want to feel safe in their neighbourhoods.
egCn: 大多数公民都是守法的，只想在自己的社区里感到安全。

eg: Bored teenagers with nothing to do are sometimes responsible for vandalism in parks.
egCn: 无所事事的青少年有时会在公园里破坏公物。

eg: The jury took two days to reach a verdict in the fraud case.
egCn: 陪审团花了两天时间才对这起诈骗案作出裁决。

eg: Prisoners who learn a skill while inside are much less likely to reoffend.
egCn: 在狱中学会一门技能的犯人再次犯罪的可能性要小得多。

eg: Journalists have a duty to check their facts before publishing a story.
egCn: 记者有责任在发表报道前核实事实。

eg: I read an interesting article about how schools in Finland teach reading.
egCn: 我读了一篇有趣的文章，讲芬兰的学校如何教阅读。

eg: Many readers only look at the headlines and never read the full story.
egCn: 许多读者只看标题，从不读完整篇报道。

eg: Advertisements aimed at children should be banned during family viewing hours.
egCn: 在家庭收视时段，应禁止播放针对儿童的广告。

eg: With hundreds of channels available, family members rarely watch the same programme together.
egCn: 有数百个频道可选，家人很少一起看同一个节目。

eg: A reporter was sent to the flooded village to interview local residents.
egCn: 一名记者被派往被淹的村庄采访当地居民。

cn: （电视、广播节目）主持人；陈述者
eg: The presenter asked both politicians the same difficult questions on live television.
egCn: 主持人在电视直播中向两位政客提出了同样尖锐的问题。

eg: Watching a good documentary can teach you more than reading a dull textbook.
egCn: 看一部好的纪录片比读一本枯燥的课本能学到更多。

eg: Television should offer education as well as entertainment to its viewers.
egCn: 电视既应为观众提供娱乐，也应提供教育。

eg: My grandmother has watched the same soap opera every evening for twenty years.
egCn: 我奶奶二十年来每晚都看同一部肥皂剧。

eg: The editor decided not to print the photos because they might upset readers.
egCn: 主编决定不刊登这些照片，因为它们可能让读者不安。

eg: Young people often copy the fashion and lifestyle of their favourite celebrities.
egCn: 年轻人常常模仿自己喜爱的明星的穿着和生活方式。

eg: The final was broadcast live to millions of viewers around the world.
egCn: 决赛向全球数百万观众进行了现场直播。

eg: The press has a responsibility to report the news fairly and accurately.
egCn: 新闻界有责任公正准确地报道新闻。

eg: The programme attracts a large audience of teenagers on Saturday evenings.
egCn: 这档节目每周六晚吸引大批青少年观众。

eg: Viewers complained that the news report showed too much violence.
egCn: 观众投诉这则新闻报道展示了过多暴力画面。

eg: Some magazines are full of celebrity gossip rather than serious news.
egCn: 有些杂志满是名人八卦，而不是严肃新闻。

eg: Many viewers switch to another channel as soon as the commercials begin.
egCn: 广告一开始，许多观众就换台了。

eg: Large companies often sponsor sports events to improve their public image.
egCn: 大公司常常赞助体育赛事来改善公众形象。

cn: 新闻业；新闻工作；新闻报道
eg: Good journalism holds powerful people responsible for their actions.
egCn: 优秀的新闻报道能让有权势的人为自己的行为负责。

eg: The mass media play a powerful role in shaping public opinion.
egCn: 大众传媒在塑造公众舆论方面发挥着强大作用。

eg: The scandal brought the company a lot of negative publicity.
egCn: 这起丑闻给公司带来了大量负面报道。

eg: Readers should compare several sources because some newspapers are clearly biased.
egCn: 读者应该比较多个来源，因为有些报纸明显带有偏见。

eg: She writes a weekly column about family life for a national newspaper.
egCn: 她为一家全国性报纸撰写关于家庭生活的每周专栏。

eg: The film was praised by critics but failed to attract large audiences.
egCn: 这部电影受到评论家的称赞，却没能吸引大批观众。

eg: Newspapers sometimes exaggerate the risks of crime to sell more copies.
egCn: 报纸有时为了多卖几份而夸大犯罪的风险。

eg: Most people now learn about breaking news through their phones rather than television.
egCn: 如今大多数人通过手机而不是电视获知突发新闻。

eg: A short, catchy slogan helps people remember a product.
egCn: 简短上口的广告语能帮人记住一个产品。

eg: The minister resigned after a scandal involving public money.
egCn: 这位部长因一起涉及公款的丑闻而辞职。

eg: Television coverage of the election focused more on personalities than on policies.
egCn: 电视对选举的报道更关注候选人的个人形象而非政策。

eg: Tabloids often publish private photos of celebrities without their permission.
egCn: 小报经常未经允许就刊登名人的私人照片。

eg: Some argue that a degree of censorship is needed to protect children from harmful content.
egCn: 有人认为，需要一定程度的审查来保护儿童免受有害内容的影响。

eg: During the war, both sides used posters and radio as tools of propaganda.
egCn: 战争期间，双方都把海报和广播当作宣传工具。

eg: Mainstream newspapers sometimes ignore stories that matter to minority groups.
egCn: 主流报纸有时会忽略对少数群体重要的新闻。

cn: 耸人听闻的；轰动的；极好的
eg: Sensational headlines attract readers but often give a false picture of events.
egCn: 耸人听闻的标题能吸引读者，却常常歪曲事件真相。

eg: Advertisements that make misleading claims about health benefits should be banned.
egCn: 对健康益处作出误导性宣传的广告应被禁止。

eg: Programmes shown at prime time attract the most viewers and the highest advertising fees.
egCn: 在黄金时段播出的节目吸引观众最多，广告费也最高。

eg: Taking photos of famous people in their own homes is a serious invasion of privacy.
egCn: 在名人自己家中偷拍照片是对隐私的严重侵犯。
collocations: complain of an invasion of privacy

cn: 大报；严肃报纸（与小报相对）
eg: Broadsheets tend to offer deeper analysis of political issues than tabloids do.
egCn: 与小报相比，大报往往对政治议题有更深入的分析。

cn: 监督者；监督机构；看门狗
eg: A free press acts as a watchdog that keeps an eye on those in power.
egCn: 自由的新闻界充当着监督当权者的角色。

eg: Young people are less likely to vote in elections than older generations.
egCn: 年轻人在选举中投票的可能性低于年长一代。

eg: Some people think sixteen-year-olds should be allowed to vote in national elections.
egCn: 有些人认为应该允许十六岁的人在全国选举中投票。

eg: Many voters feel that politicians break their promises once they are elected.
egCn: 许多选民觉得政客一旦当选就会违背承诺。

cn: 政治的；政党的；关心政治的
eg: Social media has changed the way political parties communicate with voters.
egCn: 社交媒体改变了政党与选民沟通的方式。

eg: Higher taxes on the rich could pay for better public schools and hospitals.
egCn: 对富人征收更高的税可以用来改善公立学校和医院。

eg: Every citizen has a responsibility to obey the law and pay taxes.
egCn: 每位公民都有遵纪守法和纳税的责任。

eg: The education minister promised to reduce class sizes in primary schools.
egCn: 教育部长承诺缩小小学的班级规模。

eg: The new law must be approved by parliament before it comes into force.
egCn: 新法律必须经议会批准后才能生效。

eg: The government launched a campaign to persuade more young people to register to vote.
egCn: 政府发起了一场运动，劝说更多年轻人登记成为选民。

eg: Thousands of students joined a peaceful protest against the rise in university fees.
egCn: 数千名学生参加了反对大学学费上涨的和平抗议活动。

cn: 民主；民主制度；民主国家
eg: In a healthy democracy, people can criticise the government without fear.
egCn: 在健全的民主制度中，人们可以无所畏惧地批评政府。

eg: In most large cities, residents elect a new mayor every four years.
egCn: 在大多数大城市，居民每四年选举一次新市长。

eg: Many taxpayers object to their money being spent on expensive public art.
egCn: 许多纳税人反对把他们的钱花在昂贵的公共艺术上。

eg: A strong welfare system protects people who lose their jobs or become ill.
egCn: 健全的福利制度为失业或患病的人提供保障。

eg: The government has cut the arts budget to spend more on public transport.
egCn: 政府削减了艺术预算，以便在公共交通上投入更多。

eg: Taxes pay for public services such as schools, hospitals and rubbish collection.
egCn: 税收用于支付学校、医院和垃圾清运等公共服务。

eg: Many teachers support reform of the exam system but disagree about the details.
egCn: 许多教师支持考试制度改革，但在细节上意见不一。

eg: Police were called when the demonstration outside parliament became violent.
egCn: 议会外的示威游行演变为暴力冲突，警方随即被叫到现场。

cn: 反对派；反对；（the Opposition）反对党
eg: The opposition criticised the plan, saying it would hurt low-income families.
egCn: 反对党批评这项计划，称其会伤害低收入家庭。

eg: Government officials should explain clearly how public money is being spent.
egCn: 政府官员应清楚说明公共资金是如何使用的。

eg: Freedom of expression is regarded as one of the most basic human rights.
egCn: 言论自由被视为最基本的人权之一。

eg: Freedom of speech does not give people the right to spread hatred.
egCn: 言论自由并不赋予人们传播仇恨的权利。

eg: The dictator controlled the newspapers and put his critics in prison.
egCn: 这名独裁者控制了报纸，并把批评他的人关进监狱。

eg: The local council has decided to close two libraries to save money.
egCn: 地方议会已决定关闭两家图书馆以节省开支。

eg: Older voters are more likely than younger ones to turn up on election day.
egCn: 年长选民比年轻选民更有可能在选举日去投票。

eg: Parliament passed a law banning smoking in all public buildings.
egCn: 议会通过了一项在所有公共建筑内禁烟的法律。

eg: Cuts in public spending have led to longer waiting times in hospitals.
egCn: 公共开支的削减导致医院候诊时间延长。

eg: A country cannot be governed well if its leaders ignore ordinary people.
egCn: 如果领导人无视普通百姓，国家就无法得到良好治理。

eg: The Ministry of Education plans to introduce free school meals for all children.
egCn: 教育部计划为所有儿童提供免费校餐。

eg: In a republic, the head of state is elected rather than born into the role.
egCn: 在共和制国家，国家元首是选出来的，而不是世袭的。

eg: The constitution guarantees every adult citizen the right to vote.
egCn: 宪法保障每位成年公民的选举权。

eg: Corruption among officials wastes public money and destroys trust in government.
egCn: 官员腐败浪费公共资金，并摧毁人们对政府的信任。

cn: 官僚作风；繁文缛节；官僚机构
eg: Too much bureaucracy makes it hard for small businesses to get started.
egCn: 过多的繁文缛节让小企业难以起步。

eg: The country held a referendum to decide whether to change its voting system.
egCn: 该国举行全民公投，决定是否改变选举制度。

eg: Some politicians want to abolish university fees and fund higher education through taxes.
egCn: 一些政客希望废除大学学费，改由税收资助高等教育。

eg: Civil servants must remain neutral whichever party is in power.
egCn: 无论哪个党执政，公务员都必须保持中立。

eg: Elections are held by secret ballot so that nobody can be pressured into voting a certain way.
egCn: 选举采用无记名投票，这样谁也不会被迫按某种方式投票。

eg: The regime banned foreign newspapers and blocked access to independent news.
egCn: 该政权禁止外国报纸，并屏蔽独立新闻来源。

eg: Fair taxation means that those who earn more contribute a larger share.
egCn: 公平的税制意味着挣得多的人要承担更大的份额。

eg: The party failed to convince the electorate that its plans were affordable.
egCn: 该党未能让选民相信其计划在财政上负担得起。

eg: Spring Festival is the most important time of year for families in China.
egCn: 春节是中国家庭一年中最重要的时节。

eg: People in my hometown celebrate the harvest with music, dancing and a big meal.
egCn: 我家乡的人们用音乐、舞蹈和一顿大餐来庆祝丰收。

eg: It is a local custom to remove your shoes before entering someone's home.
egCn: 进别人家前脱鞋是当地的习俗。

eg: Free entry to museums and galleries encourages more people to enjoy art.
egCn: 博物馆和美术馆免费开放能吸引更多人欣赏艺术。

eg: The museum is holding an exhibition of ancient Egyptian jewellery this summer.
egCn: 这家博物馆今年夏天将举办古埃及珠宝展。

eg: Religion still plays an important part in daily life in many countries.
egCn: 在许多国家，宗教仍然在日常生活中扮演着重要角色。

eg: We should respect other people's beliefs even when we do not share them.
egCn: 即使不认同，我们也应尊重他人的信仰。

cn: （特定时期或民族的）服装；戏服
eg: During the festival, dancers wear colourful costumes that represent different regions.
egCn: 节日期间，舞者们身着代表不同地区的多彩服装。

eg: Visiting ancient temples helps young people understand their country's long history.
egCn: 参观古老的寺庙能帮助年轻人了解本国悠久的历史。

cn: 纪念碑；纪念馆；历史遗迹
eg: The city spends a lot of money protecting its historic monuments.
egCn: 这座城市花大量资金保护其历史古迹。

eg: Studying literature helps students understand how people lived and thought in the past.
egCn: 学习文学能帮助学生了解过去的人们如何生活和思考。

eg: Children in my country learn classical poetry by heart in primary school.
egCn: 在我们国家，孩子们在小学就背诵古典诗歌。

eg: The wedding ceremony lasted three days and involved the whole village.
egCn: 这场婚礼持续了三天，全村人都参与其中。

eg: A large modern sculpture was placed in the square, but many residents disliked it.
egCn: 广场上放置了一座大型现代雕塑，但许多居民并不喜欢。

cn: 有历史意义的；历史上著名的
eg: The historic old town attracts thousands of visitors every weekend.
egCn: 这座历史悠久的古城每个周末都吸引成千上万的游客。

eg: My grandfather still sings the folk songs he learned as a boy.
egCn: 我爷爷至今还会唱他小时候学会的民歌。

eg: Traditional crafts such as weaving are disappearing as young people move to cities.
egCn: 随着年轻人迁往城市，织布等传统手艺正在消失。

eg: According to local legend, the lake was created by a dragon's tears.
egCn: 根据当地传说，这座湖是由龙的眼泪形成的。

eg: Sichuan cuisine is famous around the world for its hot and spicy flavours.
egCn: 川菜以香辣口味闻名世界。

eg: Many old superstitions, like avoiding the number four, still influence people's choices today.
egCn: 许多古老的迷信，比如避开数字四，至今仍影响着人们的选择。

eg: In this village, people have worshipped at the same temple for six hundred years.
egCn: 在这个村子里，人们六百年来一直在同一座寺庙祭拜。

eg: The painting was ignored for years before critics recognised it as a masterpiece.
egCn: 这幅画被冷落多年后，评论家才认识到它是一件杰作。

eg: Charles Dickens was a novelist who wrote about the lives of the poor.
egCn: 查尔斯·狄更斯是一位描写穷人生活的小说家。

eg: The young playwright's first play was performed at a small theatre in London.
egCn: 这位年轻剧作家的处女作在伦敦一家小剧院上演。

eg: During the festival, families visit graves to remember their ancestors.
egCn: 节日期间，各家去扫墓，缅怀祖先。

eg: The museum explains how ancient civilisations developed writing and farming.
egCn: 博物馆讲解古代文明如何发展出文字和农业。

eg: Thousands of people lined the streets to watch the National Day parade.
egCn: 成千上万的人站在街道两旁观看国庆游行。

eg: People of different faiths can live together peacefully if they respect each other.
egCn: 只要相互尊重，不同信仰的人可以和平共处。

eg: The gallery displays portraits of famous writers from the nineteenth century.
egCn: 这家美术馆展出十九世纪著名作家的肖像。

cn: 双语的；能说两种语言的
eg: Children who grow up bilingual often find it easier to learn a third language.
egCn: 从小说两种语言长大的孩子往往更容易学会第三种语言。

eg: Old buildings are part of our cultural heritage and should not be knocked down.
egCn: 老建筑是我们文化遗产的一部分，不应被拆除。

eg: Making tea for guests is an important daily ritual in many cultures.
egCn: 为客人沏茶在许多文化中是一种重要的日常仪式。

eg: Visitors should learn the basic etiquette of a country before they travel there.
egCn: 游客在出行前应了解目的地国家的基本礼仪。

eg: Different attitudes towards technology have widened the generation gap in many families.
egCn: 对科技的不同态度加深了许多家庭的代沟。

eg: In some cultures, talking about money at dinner is still a social taboo.
egCn: 在一些文化中，吃饭时谈钱仍是社交禁忌。

cn: （历史）文物；人工制品；手工艺品
eg: Many museums are being asked to return artefacts that were taken from other countries.
egCn: 许多博物馆被要求归还从其他国家带走的文物。

eg: Government funding for the performing arts helps keep ticket prices affordable.
egCn: 政府对表演艺术的资助有助于让票价保持在可承受范围内。

eg: Taking part in local festivals gives people a strong sense of belonging.
egCn: 参加当地节庆活动能给人们带来强烈的归属感。

cn: 神圣的；宗教的；受尊重的
eg: The mountain is sacred to local people, so climbing it is forbidden.
egCn: 这座山在当地人心中是神圣的，所以禁止攀登。

eg: Many children's stories have their roots in old folklore about animals and spirits.
egCn: 许多儿童故事都源自关于动物和神灵的古老民间传说。
